full_judgment: 7. The prayers in the writ petition as quoted hereinbefore shows that it combined both writ of certiorari and writ of mandamus and the subject matter of the writ petition involved the right of the writ petitioners to an immovable property, so the writ petition primafacie shows that it was a civil proceedings. It does not require any elaboration for the legal proposition that the proceedings under article 102 of the Constitution is a summary one and is decided on the statements made on affidavits filed by the parties and the documents annexed to the writ petition, the affidavit-in-opposition or any other affidavit, such as, affidavit-in-reply, supplementary affidavit are described as annexures which are called affidavit evidence. And in case of a writ petition, the principles of Order VI of the Code of Civil Procedure (the Code) is applicable and all the necessary facts are to be pleaded therein. As the dispute is to be decided mainly on affidavit, it is necessary to state the essential facts to make out a case for interference and except mentioning the grounds, the statements need not be argumentative and the pleading must be straight and clear. The same rule applies in respect of affidavit-in-opposition, but in case of a civil suit/civil case, the plaint/the application and the written statement/written objection shall contain facts only and not the evidence by which they are to be proved, but in the writ petition and the affidavit-in-opposition not only the facts but also the evidence in proof of the facts need be pleaded and annexed. The statements made in the writ petition should be controverted by filing affidavit-in-opposition and if any statement in the writ petition is not controverted in the affidavit-in-the respondent. Of course, the initial burden of proof of the statements made in the writ petition is on the writ petitioner who is supposed to bring sufficient materials on record in support of his case.
